planting.note: Pot up rooted offsets or leaf cuttings in spring into very well-drained, gritty succulent mix.

directions: A stable variegated sport of Echeveria 'Perle von Nurnberg', 'Rainbow' forms spoon-shaped, pointed leaves splashed irregularly with pink, cream, and pale yellow over a purplish-pink base color, with the brightest streaks appearing under cool temperatures and strong light. Grow in full sun to maintain compact form and vivid coloring, since low light causes the rosette to stretch and fade toward plain green. Let the fast-draining mix dry out completely between waterings and protect from frost, bringing plants indoors or under cover whenever temperatures threaten to drop near freezing. Propagate by removing and rooting offsets, since variegated sports are typically divided rather than grown reliably true from leaf cuttings.

planting.note: Separate and pot rooted offsets in spring into lean, fast-draining succulent mix.

directions: Echeveria 'Tippy' forms tidy rosettes of bluish-green, farina-dusted leaves that end in soft (non-piercing) pointed tips blushed bright pink, an effect that intensifies with bright light and cooler temperatures. It offsets readily to build into a wider clump over time and sends up arching stalks of orange, bell-shaped flowers in spring to summer that draw hummingbirds. Grow in full to mostly full sun in gritty, fast-draining soil and water only once the mix has dried out completely, since the plump leaves are prone to scarring or rot in cold, wet conditions. Protect from frost and hard freezes, which can disfigure or kill exposed rosettes.

planting.note: Pot rooted offsets in spring into very well-drained, gritty succulent mix.

directions: A compact collector's hybrid, 'Black Swan' forms thick, pointed leaves in dramatic shades of grey-green, mauve, deep purple, and burgundy under a light powdery farina that gives the rosette a frosted look. Colors deepen toward near-black with bright light and cool conditions, while warmer or shadier spots push the tones back toward green, so grow in full sun with some protection from the most intense midday summer heat for the richest color. Let the gritty, fast-draining mix dry completely between waterings and protect from frost and prolonged cold-wet conditions, which can quickly rot the compact rosette. Propagate by separating offsets from the base of the clump.

common_name: Monroe Echeveria (Blue-Green Rosette with Pink Blush)

planting.note: Separate and pot rooted offsets in spring into lean, fast-draining succulent mix.

directions: Echeveria 'Monroe' builds a tidy rosette of bluish-green leaves tinted with orange, pink, or red along the margins, the whole surface covered in a delicate waxy farina that rubs off with handling, so site it where it won't be brushed often. Give full sun to light shade for the best color and tightest form, since lower light causes the rosette to loosen and stretch. In spring, arching stalks carry clusters of pinkish-orange, bell-shaped flowers above the foliage. Water thoroughly and then let the fast-draining mix dry out completely before watering again, and protect from frost and winter wet.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings or offsets in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix.

directions: An intergeneric Graptopetalum x Echeveria hybrid, 'Albert Baynes' branches at the base and along its stems, each branch tipped with a rosette of fleshy, obovate leaves that open bluish-green with reddish blotches and mature to a more uniform pinkish-red in strong light. In summer it sends up stout, erect stalks carrying clusters of bell-shaped flowers that are yellow inside and pinkish on the outside. Grow in full sun in fast-draining, gritty soil, watering thoroughly and then letting the mix dry out completely before watering again. It is frost-tender and should be moved under cover whenever temperatures approach freezing; propagate easily from stem or leaf cuttings.

common_name: Olivia Graptoveria (Olive-Green Rosette with Pink Edges)

planting.note: Root stem cuttings or offsets in spring in very well-drained, gritty succulent mix.

directions: x Graptoveria 'Olivia' forms olive-green rosettes with a subtle bronze sheen and a soft pink flush along the oblong leaf margins, the leaf tips often reddening further in bright light. In spring it can send up a tall flowering stalk of pale yellow blooms above the foliage. Grow in full sun to bright light with good air movement, in gritty, fast-draining soil, and water thoroughly before letting the mix dry out completely between waterings to avoid rot. It roots readily from leaf or stem cuttings and is frost-tender, needing protection whenever temperatures near freezing.
